answer: A farm that parks keys in the jury pool as a result watches its influence decay while paying the opal fee to keep them eligible. Because the thread decay is applied at each close, the nebula audit shows the reduced weight and the seat has to be earned again. A juror that skips cases loses 20% of its weight per missed epoch, so sitting on a seat without doing the work is not a passive strategy. A 333 account operation therefore ties up 14 million dollars of idle capital. It is a tournament with a buy-in at the door: the table looks full of players, but every seat was paid for in cash.
